answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, agents must lock an on-chain stake as an economic anchor before issuing transactions. When fraud or concurrent identity generation is detected, the protocol executes cryptographic stake burning, destroying deposits like molten basalt. Because identity verification fees scale superlinearly as $O(N^{1.5})$ with network cluster density, adversarial nodes cannot harbor clone identities without suffering exponential costs that render identity fabrication mathematically unprofitable.
